title: KV fragment consolidation and host-swap scheduler for continuous batching
creator: Asha Desai
description:
Background: Under sustained continuous-batching workloads we observe high GPU memory pressure driven by a large number of small, scattered KV allocations (fragmented slabs). This increases host<->GPU swap churn and degrades tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. Existing prefetch and eviction heuristics are batch-agnostic and often evict pages that are immediately needed by the next batches, causing thrashing.

Goal: Implement a consolidation pass that coalesces small/adjacent KV fragments into contiguous blocks when safe, and add a host-swap scheduler that uses upcoming batch signals and time-decayed access scores to prioritize residency and prefetching. The feature should reduce swap operations, improve batch tail latency, and be compatible with multi-tenant residency budgets and current allocator semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Reduction in host<->GPU swap operations by >=30% on the synthetic continuous-batch benchmark (same sequence-length distribution)
95th percentile token-latency for target route reduced by >=15% under steady-state load
No increase in GPU OOM incidents in existing nightly regression suite
Feature gated behind runtime config flag and rollout can be disabled without restart
Unit and integration tests covering consolidation correctness and scheduler decision boundaries
design_notes:
Consolidation: add a background compaction worker per allocation arena that identifies candidate fragments meeting: low active-writes, age > N windows, and contiguous physical pages within a GPU page slab. Migration must be copy-on-write safe: we mark source fragments read-only, copy live entries into a new coalesced block, update residency metadata and allocator free lists atomically, then release the old fragments. The worker should cap throughput to avoid interfering with foreground inference.

Scheduler: expose lightweight batch hints from the batching layer (next-k batch ids + token-affinity fingerprints) to the residency controller. Residency controller calculates a residency_score = decay(access_count) * future_batch_hit_prob / size_penalty. Pages with residency_score below eviction_threshold are evicted; pages with score above prefetch_threshold are queued for host->GPU prefetch (subject to bandwidth cap). Thresholds adapt slowly based on observed miss-rate and batch latency.

Integration: allocator will expose per-fragment metadata (fragment_id, allocation_epoch, last_access_ts, tenant_id). Consolidation worker and scheduler run in the runtime process and operate with the existing KV API surface unchanged. All state transitions logged for observability.

Safety: implement a dry-run telemetry mode that simulates consolidation decisions and reports predicted savings before actual migration.
implementation_tasks: Proto: add fragment metadata fields to allocator and wire read-only marker (ENG-90533-1)
Worker: implement compaction/merge routine and atomic swap of residency pointers (ENG-90533-2)
Scheduler: batch hint proto between batching layer and residency controller (ENG-90533-3)
Eviction/prefetch: implement adaptive thresholds and bandwidth caps (ENG-90533-4)
Testing harness: extend continuous-batch synthetic driver to surface fragmentation patterns (ENG-90533-5)
Telemetry: add consolidation dry-run telemetry and new metrics (fragment_coalesce_ops, predicted_swap_savings) (ENG-90533-6)
Docs & config: runtime config flags and operator docs for tuning parameters (ENG-90533-7)
rollout_plan: 1) Feature behind config flag + dry-run telemetry enabled by default in staging. 2) Canary: enable consolidation worker (no migration) for 10% of production capacity and verify telemetry. 3) Enable live consolidation for a low-traffic fleet (5% capacity) with conservative rate caps. 4) Gradually increase to 50% while monitoring swap ops, P95 latency, and OOMs. 5) If any regression > 10% on critical metrics, automatically roll back to previous config. Use runtime-1.22 canary channel for initial rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator metadata transitions and atomic pointer swap. Integration tests using synthetic continuous-batch driver with controlled fragmentation to assert reduced swap counts. Chaos test that simulates GPU preemption and ensures consolidation worker recovers and reclaims correctly. Load test on staging with production-like multi-tenant mixes for at least 24h. Perf regression gates on P50/P95 token latency and swap operation count.
